title: An objective solved on the base reads as solved in every view of the backlog: the RSI page, the overview and `spawn mission objectives` follow the integrator's record
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs (`solved_on_base`: the `objective.solved` record and the task cancelled on it); crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs (`OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS`, which counts that record as a landing, and `OBJECTIVE_MISSIONS`); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`with_objectives`, `objective_json`, `rsi_summary`); crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs (`objectives_row`, `spawn mission objectives`); web/src/rsi.ts; docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.4.

The problem. When a task's gate finds an objective's scenario already passing at the base, the integrator records `objective.solved`, cancels the task on that record, and from then on counts the objective as landed: it never assigns it again. The views of the backlog do not read that record. /api/rsi, /api/overview's RSI summary and `spawn mission objectives` count only landed tasks. So the objective stays "open", is counted open, and is named `next_objective`, "what the integrator assigns next", though the integrator never will. On the live fleet, mission 4's objective 34 was recorded solved on the base at 2026-11-08 10:51 UTC (event 109278, task 201). On 2026-11-11 the RSI page still showed it open and next, while the integrator had assigned 43, 46 and 47 after it.

Required behaviour.
(a) An objective with an `objective.solved` record in its own mission is "solved", as a landing makes it, in every view built from the backlog: /api/rsi's objective rows, `next_objective` and the counts, /api/overview's RSI summary, and `spawn mission objectives`. It is read from the record, the same one `OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS` reads, so the views and the integrator cannot disagree. A record of another mission solves nothing here.
(b) Each objective row names the record: `solved_on_base` is {"event", "task", "base"} for an objective solved this way, and null for every other one. The RSI page says so beside the objective (for example "solved on the base at <base>, task #<task>").
(c) Nothing else changes: an objective solved by a landing reads as today, its landings and metric history as before, and the owner's objectives stay "owner".

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/052.sh. It seeds a fresh database with no loop, as 043 and 049 do: control records folded by spawn_control_refold(). One objective mission (accept gate) has backlog objectives 1 to 4:
- task 1 landed objective 1;
- task 2 was cancelled on an `objective.solved` record for objective 2;
- another mission has an `objective.solved` record for its objective 3;
- task 3 is in flight on objective 4.
The checks:
- (1) /api/rsi: statuses solved, solved, open, open; objective 2's `solved_on_base` names the record, task 2 and the base, and the other rows' are null; `next_objective` 3.
- (2) /api/overview's RSI summary: open 2, solved 2, next 3.
- (3) `spawn mission objectives --mission 1`: open [3, 4], solved 2, next 3.
It fails with 1 at (1) on 351fb1e6: objective 2 reads "open".

The product reason. The RSI page and the supervisor's view of the backlog say what the integrator will do. An objective the fleet will never work on again is not shown as open and next for days.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
